title: Wide range screening of algorithmic bias in word embedding models using large sentiment lexicons reveals underreported bias types
findings: Popular word embedding models showed a consistent mild to moderate association of negative sentiment terms with the pole representing Muslims on a 'Christians to Muslims' axis. Additionally, several models displayed a negative bias against a lack of religious faith (non-religiosity/atheism).

measurement_description: The benchmark measured sentiment bias by analyzing the correlation between positive/negative sentiment words and cultural axes representing religious groups. Specifically, it evaluated associations on a 'Christians to Muslims' axis and a 'religiosity' axis (Christian/Muslim vs. atheist/nonreligious).
